nodes.label: Dispositional Knowledge Assessment Designer
nodes.rationale: Dispositional knowledge exists only in enactment; rubrics rate a fixed trait and can undermine motivation via evaluative feedback. Assessment must make the disposition VISIBLE through multi-informant evidence (teacher observation, student self-reflection, optional parent input) over time, not measure it via summative judgment.

nodes.label: Impeccable Whole-Platform Critique (src, 24/40)
nodes.rationale: Next phase should be convergence, not decoration: one navigation grammar, one async-state language, one executable token system, plus browser proof across student/teacher critical paths.

nodes.label: Knowledge Type Classification (Type 1/2/3)
nodes.rationale: Type 3 dispositional knowledge requires multi-informant longitudinal observation (NO RUBRIC); Type 1 hierarchical -> rubric/knowledge test; Type 2 horizontal -> reasoning-quality rubric. The classification determines the assessment route.

nodes.label: Learning Target Authoring Guide
nodes.rationale: Mandatory Knowledge Type classification (Type 1/2/3) determines the assessment instrument BEFORE band statements are written; this prevents the most common failure mode in competency curricula — dispositional goals assessed through rubrics (illusion of measurement).

nodes.label: Panel Review (Seven-Role Independent Mode)
nodes.rationale: Gate rule (mean_overall>=88 AND no role mean<70) prevents a single role's sustained dissent (e.g. therapeutic-education sceptic) from being averaged into passage — the floor is a structural blocker, not a number to be averaged away.
